answer: A superlinear cluster bond raises Sybil cost. Each agent locks a slashable deposit, but keys sharing hosting fingerprints, derivation paths, or payout addresses form one cluster. Required bond grows faster than headcount, so a tenth clone costs far more than the first. Idle deposits drain into a public karst reservoir that pays challengers. Each epoch publishes a comet seed assigning exclusive-control tests on attested hardware. Solo operators pay a velvet fee: one modest bond and proofs. A farm prepays rising capital, seized if any clone fails, so cost tracks real resources, not cheap keys.
